title: Homotopy-pullback test for relative coslice boundary lifting
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories, full subcategories, Kan complexes and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], sharp join coslices of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cocone-associativity], and trivial Kan fibrations of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. Let $q:C\to D$ be an inner fibration between quasicategories in one fixed sufficiently large universe. Let $j:A\hookrightarrow B$ be a degreewise injective map of small simplicial sets, let $d:B\to C$, put $e=dj$, and let $C_0\subseteq C$ be any full subcategory. For each vertex $W$ of $C_0$, suppose the square of strict apex fibers
$$\begin{array}{ccc}C_{d/}\times_C\{W\}&\longrightarrow&C_{e/}\times_C\{W\}\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
D_{qd/}\times_D\{qW\}&\longrightarrow&D_{qe/}\times_D\{qW\}\end{array}$$
is a homotopy pullback of Kan complexes. All maps here are actual restrictions along $j$ or postcomposition by $q$. A homotopy pullback means that the map from the upper-left corner to the space of a point in the upper-right corner, a point in the lower-left corner, and a path between their images in the lower-right corner, with all higher simplices retained, is a weak homotopy equivalence; for this strictly commuting square use the constant path. Then the actual restriction map
$$C_0\times_C C_{d/}\longrightarrow C_0\times_C\bigl(C_{e/}\times_{D_{qe/}}D_{qd/}\bigr)$$
is a trivial Kan fibration: every prescribed simplex boundary and every prescribed target simplex lift with both restriction and projection equalities, including dimension zero. The apex projections in these pullbacks restrict to the last join block. There is no hypothesis on objects of $C$ outside $C_0$, no colimit-existence hypothesis, and $A$, $B$ or $C_0$ may be empty.

proof.text: Put $X=C_{d/}$ and $T=C_{e/}\times_{D_{qe/}}D_{qd/}$. Apply [lem-cbc-relative-coslice-left-fibration] to $(q,j,d)$: its actual map $\rho:X\to T$, $h\mapsto(h|_{A\star\Delta^n},qh)$, is a left fibration over the common apex map to $C$. Put $X_0=C_0\times_CX$ and $T_0=C_0\times_CT$. Then $\rho_0:X_0\to T_0$ is the pullback of $\rho$ along $T_0\to T$. It is a left fibration: project any lifting problem to $T$, lift using $\rho$, and pair the lifted simplex with the prescribed $C_0$-coordinate. The apex equality holds because $\rho$ preserves the last join block. This directly verifies the pullback lifting assertion using [def-coef-infinity-fibrations].

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.8; pullback lifting argument, with the apex map from Proposition 4.4.2.13.

proof.text: We will use the left-handed version of [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber]. Explicitly, reverse simplex operators by $\alpha:[m]\to[n]\mapsto(i\mapsto n-\alpha(m-i))$. This preserves degreewise pullbacks, takes $\Lambda_i^n$ to $\Lambda_{n-i}^n$, and takes left fibrations to right fibrations by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. By [lem-coef-infinity-opposite-subdivision-kan-zigzag], the opposite of a Kan complex is Kan. Thus for a left fibration $L\to S$ with Kan base $S$, apply [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber] to $L^{\mathrm{op}}\to S^{\mathrm{op}}$ and reverse each horn filler back. This proves that $L\to S$ is a Kan fibration and $L$ is Kan. This is just the opposite specialization of the cited theorem, not an assumption on a quasicategory base.

source.place: Corollary 4.4.3.8, left-handed version of the existing right-fibration node.

proof.text: Fix a vertex $W$ of $C_0$, and write $X_W=C_{d/}\times_C\{W\}$, $U_W=C_{e/}\times_C\{W\}$, $V_W=D_{qd/}\times_D\{qW\}$ and $Z_W=D_{qe/}\times_D\{qW\}$. These are Kan by the hypothesis. Apply [lem-cbc-relative-coslice-left-fibration] with inner fibration $D\to\Delta^0$, the same $j$, and diagram $qd$. Its relative restriction is precisely $D_{qd/}\to D_{qe/}$, since both coslices in the terminal simplicial set are terminal. Pull it back along $Z_W\to D_{qe/}$. The resulting map is $r_W:V_W\to Z_W$: a simplex with prescribed apex equal to the constant simplex at $qW$ still has that apex after restriction. Pullback left-horn lifting follows by pairing with the prescribed base simplex as in step 1, using [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Step 2 applies since $Z_W$ is Kan, so $r_W$ is a Kan fibration.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.8 for D to the terminal quasicategory; Corollary 4.4.3.8 for the Kan-base specialization.

proof.text: In degree $n$, a simplex of $T$ over the constant apex $W$ is exactly a pair $(u,v)\in(U_W)_n\times(V_W)_n$ satisfying $qu=v|_{A\star\Delta^n}$. Hence the strict apex fiber is the degreewise pullback $P_W=U_W\times_{Z_W}V_W$, and $\rho$ on apex fibers is $f_W:X_W\to P_W$. The map $P_W\to U_W$ is a Kan fibration by step 3: a horn lift is obtained by keeping its prescribed $U_W$-simplex and filling its $V_W$-coordinate against $r_W$. Since $U_W$ is Kan, first filling a projected horn in $U_W$ and then lifting it proves that $P_W$ is Kan. Moreover $f_W$ is a pullback of $\rho$ along $P_W\to T$, so is a left fibration by the paired-coordinate argument of step 1. Step 2 now makes $f_W$ a Kan fibration. All these are literal coordinate identifications of the degreewise pullbacks in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with the lifting properties of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations].

source.place: Corollary 4.4.3.8 and degreewise pullback identifications; agent calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] to $U_W\to Z_W\leftarrow V_W$. All three objects are Kan, and the second leg $r_W$ is a Kan fibration by step 3. The constant-path map $c_W:P_W\to P(U_W\to Z_W\leftarrow V_W)$ is consequently a weak homotopy equivalence. Its composite $c_Wf_W$ is exactly the comparison in the hypothesis: it sends $h$ to $(h|_{A\star\Delta^n},qh)$ and the constant path at their common restriction. That composite is a weak homotopy equivalence by assumption. Therefore $f_W$ is a weak homotopy equivalence: on components and every based homotopy group its induced map is the inverse of the isomorphism induced by $c_W$, followed by the isomorphism induced by $c_Wf_W$, in the conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.7 and the constant-path model of Construction 3.4.0.3; two-out-of-three checked on homotopy groups.

proof.text: For a vertex $t$ of $T_0$, let $W\in C_0$ be its apex. Under step 4 it is a vertex of $P_W$. Steps 4 and 5 show that $f_W:X_W\to P_W$ is a Kan fibration and a weak homotopy equivalence. By [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion], its strict fiber at $t$ is a contractible Kan complex. This fiber is literally $(X_0)_t=\{t\}\times_{T_0}X_0$: prescribing $t$ already prescribes the $C_0$-coordinate $W$ and both of its compatible cocones. Thus every vertex fiber of $\rho_0$ is a weakly contractible Kan complex, without testing any apex outside $C_0$.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.2.14: identification of the vertex fibers for the contractible-fiber test.

proof.text: Reverse simplex operators as in step 2. Since $\rho_0$ is a left fibration, $\rho_0^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a right fibration by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Its vertex fibers are the opposites of the fibers in step 6; they are Kan and weakly contractible by the preservation of Kan complexes and weak homotopy equivalences in [lem-coef-infinity-opposite-subdivision-kan-zigzag]. Apply [lem-coef-right-fibration-contractible-fibers] to conclude that $\rho_0^{\mathrm{op}}$ lifts all simplex boundaries. Opposite takes $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ to the same boundary inclusion under reversal of the ordered vertices. Reversing each such lift gives an exact lift for $\rho_0$, including $n=0$, where the boundary is empty. By [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], this is the asserted trivial Kan fibration. Every restriction and projection equality is preserved because all reversals and pullbacks were simplicial. If $C_0$ is empty both sides are empty and no lifting problem has a target simplex. Empty $A$ or $B$ causes no change in the relative-coslice theorem or in any degreewise calculation above.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.2.14 (2) implies (1), by the existing right-handed criterion and explicit opposite symmetry.
